answer: Neighborhood Closure Scoring. Each agent is scored by the overlap between the sets of peers its peers connect to; a node whose neighbor neighborhoods share almost no edges is treated as isolated and its messages stop propagating. To pass, an attacker must wire each fake identity into the real graph so its neighbors' peer sets overlap, which means buying genuine connections or paying the jade cost of maintaining many live sessions.
